newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares seen levelling out after major gains.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares seen levelling out after major gains.

text.p: Danish share prices soared to near-record levels on Thursday underpinned by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments in Senate but dealers expected an already nervous market to run out of steam and flatten out ahead of the weekend.
"After the index climbed almost three points today, the market must surely level out tomorrow," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index finished 2.79 point up at 158.43, not far short of February 20's record all-time closing high of 159.12. The KFX March future rose 1.95 point to 157.55 with 495 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

The strong dollar also helped the market on with dollar-sensitive Novo Nordisk closing 24 crowns up at 684. Leading banks Den Danske and Unidanmark also went ahead, the former ending 13 crowns up at 600 and the latter 14 crowns higher at 350.

Codan closed 15 crowns ahead at 960 after posting a solid rise in 1996 pre-profits while Copenhagen Airports, which announced 1996 profits below market expectations due to high costs, finished unchanged at 685 after hitting a high of 690.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.192 billion crowns.
